memory_lessons.applicability: Per-axis coordinate reuse on this kernel should be judged end-to-end, including allocation and accesses; saving repeated arithmetic alone is not sufficient evidence of benefit.
memory_lessons.claim: The xy lattice/fraction-only candidate was correct on the supplied eight cases, but its measured mean (0.3813 s) exceeded the baseline mean (0.3109 s); two samples were near 0.297 s and one was 0.549 s, so the comparison is noisy and does not isolate the cause.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure the separately identified candidate that also caches smooth weights and shared z state, using the fixed tolerance at n=768 and smaller or shifted bounds.

proposal.hypothesis: Extending the earlier xy lattice/fraction cache to also cache smooth weights and the shared per-octave z decomposition may save enough repeated weight and z-coordinate work to offset the larger per-axis state and its allocation/access traffic. This is a distinct full-state stage; no speedup is assumed.

retained: Replace per-pixel coordinate decomposition with per-axis, per-octave cached lattice cells, fractions, and smooth weights for x and y.
Cache each octave's z cell/fraction/weight and amplitude, preserving the original lambda/o progression and per-pixel accumulation order.
Preserve x0 + i * dx and y0 + j * dy before lambda multiplication, and allocate/access all scratch state within noise_serial so its cost is timed.
